title: New Zealand's Ruling Coalition Loses Parliamentary Majority in Final Count, Zelenskyy Warns of Mass Russian Strike as Trump Urges Putin to Pull Back, and Kuwait Drone Attack Kills Two Italian Technicians
subhead: Final vote tallies leave Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's bloc one seat shy of a majority in Wellington, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warns of an imminent large-scale Russian bombardment as Donald Trump presses Vladimir Putin to de-escalate, and a fatal drone strike on an air defense site in Kuwait kills two Italian defense contractors.

sections.heading: New Zealand's Ruling Coalition Falls One Seat Short of Parliamentary Majority in Final Election Count
sections.body:
Final certified results from New Zealand's general election stripped Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's center-right governing coalition of its parliamentary majority after special and overseas ballots were tallied, BBC, AP News, and TRT World report. The ruling bloc — led by Luxon's National Party alongside coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First — finished with 65 of the 130 seats in Parliament, one seat short of the 66 required to govern outright, while the opposition center-left bloc led by the Labour Party also failed to secure a majority.

With Parliament deadlocked at 65–65, Luxon must now negotiate confidence-and-supply backing or a formal coalition arrangement with the centrist Opportunity Party, which entered Parliament as the decisive kingmaker. The razor-thin outcome complicates Wellington's fiscal austerity program and defense modernization commitments under its Indo-Pacific security partnerships.
sections.whyItMatters: Losing an outright majority on special votes forces New Zealand's National-led government into reliance on a centrist kingmaker party, slowing fiscal and foreign policy decision-making in Wellington.

sections.heading: Zelenskyy Warns of Imminent Mass Russian Strike as Trump Urges Putin to 'Pull Back' in Europe
sections.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned late Thursday that intelligence assessments indicate Russia is preparing a massive combined missile and drone bombardment across Ukraine in the coming days, Reuters and Al Jazeera report. The warning came hours after Ukrainian air defenses downed 87 Russian missiles and drones in attacks that killed at least three people and further crippled power and water distribution in Kyiv.

On the diplomatic front, US President Donald Trump stated that he directly urged Russian President Vladimir Putin — whom he referred to as a 'friend' — to 'pull back all military aggression' in Europe so that a Russia-Ukraine peace agreement can be concluded rapidly, according to TRT World. Meanwhile, Poland announced plans to establish a restricted no-fly zone along its border with Ukraine, and the Russian State Duma passed its 2027–2029 federal budget on third reading, allocating 50.05 trillion rubles ($609.3 billion) to defense over the next three years.
sections.whyItMatters: Trump's personal appeal to Putin contrasts sharply with Moscow's enactment of a $609 billion three-year war budget and preparations for another large-scale winter strike on Ukraine's energy grid.

sections.heading: Drone Strike in Kuwait Kills Two Italian Defense Technicians as Trump Says Iran War Can End 'Whenever I Want'
sections.body:
A drone attack on a military facility in Kuwait on Thursday killed two Italian nationals and wounded four other personnel working as air defense technicians for the Italian subsidiary of German arms maker Rheinmetall, SCMP, CBS News, and the BBC report. The strike marks the first fatal attack inside Kuwait in months. While Western and Gulf officials blamed Iranian-linked forces and Syria expressed official solidarity with Kuwait, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Iran's General Staff categorically denied responsibility and offered a joint investigation with Kuwaiti authorities, according to Anadolu Agency.

Speaking to US troops deployed in the Gulf on Thanksgiving, President Trump declared that 'victory is at hand' in the nine-month conflict with Iran and said the war will be over 'sort of whenever I want it to be,' while claiming the United States controls 'close to 50%' of global oil and does not need Middle Eastern crude, The Hill and Al Jazeera report. Separately, Iranian diplomats confirmed that indirect mediation with Washington via Qatar and Pakistan remains active.
sections.whyItMatters: The deaths of two European defense contractors in Kuwait threaten to draw NATO members deeper into Gulf force-protection operations just as Washington and Tehran trade public bravado while maintaining backchannel talks through Doha and Islamabad.

sections.heading: EU Leaders Deadlock Over 2028–2034 Budget While Agreeing on Spain's De Cos to Lead European Central Bank
sections.body:
Leaders of the 27 European Union member states failed to reach an agreement at an extraordinary Brussels summit on the size and funding mechanisms of the bloc's 2028–2034 long-term budget, Al Jazeera and Anadolu Agency report. While the European Parliament has demanded a $2.2 trillion spending framework to finance Ukraine military aid, defense industrial capacity, and AI competitiveness, net-contributor capitals rejected new joint borrowing and spending increases.

Despite the fiscal stalemate, Eurozone leaders reached a political agreement to appoint former Bank of Spain Governor Pablo Hernandez de Cos to succeed Christine Lagarde as President of the European Central Bank (ECB), with formal confirmation scheduled for the December 17 EU summit. In Latin America, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva appointed veteran Bradesco banker Luiz Carlos Trabuco as finance minister in an effort to halt a currency and bond sell-off, the Financial Times reports.
sections.whyItMatters: Selecting a technocratic Spanish central banker to helm the ECB provides monetary continuity for the eurozone, but the collapse of EU budget talks leaves Brussels without agreed long-term financing for Ukraine and European rearmament.

sections.heading: Turkey Suspends Visa-Free Regime With Montenegro and Rejects EU Parliament Resolution on Libya Maritime Pact
sections.body:
Turkey temporarily suspended its bilateral visa exemption agreement for ordinary passport holders from Montenegro following reciprocal visa policy adjustments tied to Podgorica's European Union accession alignment, Daily Sabah reports. At the same time, the Turkish Foreign Ministry formally rejected a European Parliament resolution challenging the Turkey-Libya maritime boundary delimitation agreement, declaring that the EU holds no legal jurisdiction or sovereign competence to adjudicate maritime zones between third states, according to Anadolu Agency.

In South Asia, the BBC reports that ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina — who was sentenced to death in absentia by a Dhaka tribunal — plans to return to Bangladesh from exile in India in December, placing intense diplomatic pressure on New Delhi and raising fears of renewed street upheaval in Dhaka.
sections.whyItMatters: Ankara's firm rejection of the European Parliament's Libya resolution—coming one day after hosting eastern Libyan commander Khalifa Haftar—signals that Turkey will not allow Brussels to dilute its Eastern Mediterranean maritime legal architecture.

bottomLine: Final election counts in New Zealand left Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's coalition one seat short of a parliamentary majority, while EU leaders deadlocked in Brussels over their 2028–2034 budget even as they tapped Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos to lead the ECB. On the security front, a fatal drone strike on Italian defense technicians in Kuwait and Russia's passage of a $609 billion three-year defense budget underscore the gap between active battlefield escalation and President Trump's holiday assurances of rapid war termination.
sources: BBC, AP News, TRT World, Al Jazeera, Reuters, SCMP, CBS News, Anadolu Agency, The Hill, Financial Times, Daily Sabah
